title: The Proposal to Dig a Trench • Days of Hunger • Jabir’s Hospitality • The Night of Fear

blocks.0: The Proposal to Dig a Trench
blocks.1: Banu al-Nadir, expelled, had taken refuge in Khaybar. From there they went first to Makkah, to Quraysh; since the account of Badr and Uhud was still unsettled, Quraysh readily agreed. Then Banu al-Nadir went to Ghatafan with the same call, promising to stand beside them themselves. On learning that Quraysh had agreed, Ghatafan agreed too. An army of about ten thousand, including Quraysh, Ghatafan, Banu Asad and Banu Sulaym, set out toward Madinah. This combined army is called al-Ahzab, the confederates.{{1}}
blocks.2: On receiving the news the Prophet {{1}} sat in consultation with the Companions. Salman al-Farisi (RA) said, in Persia when we feared an enemy, we used to dig a trench around the city. The Arabs had never seen this tactic before. The Prophet {{2}} accepted the proposal.{{3}}
blocks.3: One suggestion from a foreign Companion changed Arabia’s whole way of war. The Prophet {{1}} had not shut the door to learning something new, looking not only at who is speaking but at whether the idea is useful. The north of Madinah was open, the other sides were enclosed by mountains and houses. To every ten Companions was given the duty of digging forty cubits. The Prophet {{2}} himself also dug earth, carried earth on his shoulder, so that the dust covered even the hair of his belly.{{3}}
blocks.4: Those who finished their own portion early did not sit with folded hands; they ran to help with others’ unfinished sections. This trench, three and a half miles long, was completed in this way in six days.{{1}}
blocks.5: One could have finished one’s own portion and sat with folded hands; no one would have said anything. But winning as a team and completing one’s own duty alone are not the same. While carrying earth he would recite, in the rhythm of ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA),
blocks.7: O Allah, were it not for You we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed. Send down tranquillity upon us, keep our feet firm when we meet them; they have transgressed against us, and if they want fitnah, we refuse.{{1}}
blocks.8: When a leader carries earth with his own hands and stands beside his followers, the order is not only in words. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA) used to say,
blocks.10: On the day of Uhud I was presented before the Prophet {{1}}, I was fourteen then; he did not permit me. On the day of the Trench I was presented again, I was fifteen then; he permitted me. Nafi‘ (RA) used to say, later I went to ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, he was then caliph, and told him this hadith; he said, this is indeed the boundary between the young and the grown. Then he wrote to all his officials that whoever has completed fifteen years should be counted as an adult.{{2}}
blocks.11: The same boy, a year’s gap; the first time sent back, the second time given a place in the fighting ranks. The Prophet {{1}} neither pushed anyone into risk without preparation, nor kept anyone back when he saw them prepared. Years later this same hadith reached, through Nafi‘ (RA), the caliph ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him; he made it state policy, treating fifteen years as the boundary between young and grown, writing to all officials. This is one example of how the testimony of one event becomes law many years later.
blocks.13: A freezing morning. Muhajirun and Ansar were digging earth together, carrying it on their shoulders. There were no slaves to do this work; they did everything themselves. Seeing their fatigue and hunger the Prophet {{1}} made du‘a,
blocks.15: O Allah, the real life is the life of the Hereafter; forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirun.{{1}}
blocks.18: We are the ones who pledged allegiance to Muhammad for jihad, for as long as we live.{{1}}
blocks.19: One makes du‘a for forgiveness, the other replies with a pledge. No one is asking anything of anyone; both are giving. The food was a little barley flour, the bread made of it bitter and foul-smelling, yet even that was shared among the hungry people.{{1}}
blocks.20: In the middle of digging a hard rock came up, the pickaxe was breaking, the earth was not breaking. Jabir (RA) used to say,
blocks.22: We were digging on the day of the Trench, and a hard rock came up. The Companions came to the Prophet {{1}} and said, a rocky patch has come up in the trench. He said, I am coming down. Then he stood up, his belly tied with a stone; we had not tasted any food for three days. The Prophet {{2}} took the pickaxe in his hand, struck, and the rock became like loose sand.{{3}}
blocks.23: In one narration, with each strike Salman (RA) saw a flash of light. When asked, the Prophet {{1}} said, with the first strike he was shown the palaces of Sham, with the second Persia’s al-Mada’in, with the third the gates of San‘a’; he gave the good news that victory would come in all three directions.{{2}}
blocks.24: In the darkest moment of hunger and fatigue the farthest good news seemed to arrive. Through hardship we see the light of the future, not by avoiding hardship. Abu Talhah (RA) used to say,
blocks.26: We complained of hunger to the Prophet {{1}}, and we had each tied a stone to our belly; the Prophet {{2}} lifted two stones from his belly and showed us.{{3}}
blocks.27: To be a leader means to be the hungriest, to bear hardship first.
blocks.29: Seeing this intense hunger of the Prophet {{1}}, the heart of Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA) was stirred. At home there was only one sa‘ of barley, about three and a half kilos by today’s measure. He used to say,
blocks.31: When the trench was dug, I saw intense hunger in the Prophet {{1}}. I went to my wife and asked, do you have anything? I have seen intense hunger in the Prophet {{2}}. She brought out a bag, in it a sa‘ of barley; and we had a tame young goat, I slaughtered it, my wife ground the barley, she finished when I finished; I put the meat in the pot in pieces. Then I went back to the Prophet {{3}}. My wife said, do not disgrace me before the Prophet {{4}} and his companions. I went to him and whispered, O Messenger of Allah, we have slaughtered a young goat of ours, and ground a sa‘ of barley that we had at home; come, with a few men. The Prophet {{5}} asked, how much? I said, I told him how much. He said, a lot, good; tell her, do not take the pot down, nor take the bread from the oven, until I come. Then he said, rise. The Muhajirun and Ansar stood up.{{6}}
blocks.32: Jabir (RA) then ran to his wife and said, disaster! The Prophet {{1}} is coming with all the Muhajirun and Ansar! His wife only said, did he ask how much there is? Jabir (RA) said, yes. The Prophet {{2}} entered the house and said, come in, do not crowd. Then he himself was breaking the bread, putting meat on it, covering the pot, covering the oven, delivering to everyone as much as he took out. In this way the breaking and handing out of bread went on until everyone ate their fill. Still food remained in the pot and the oven.{{3}}
blocks.33: One sa‘ of barley, one young goat. Several hundred people ate, Muhajirun and Ansar together, yet it did not run out. For the hand that gives blessing, the reckoning of little and much is not like people’s reckoning.
blocks.35: As soon as the digging of the trench around Madinah was finished, the huge army of the Ahzab came and surrounded it. The Prophet {{1}} came out with the Companions, put his back toward Mount Sal‘, put the trench between themselves and the enemy; against ten thousand only three thousand Companions.{{2}}
blocks.36: Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the expelled leader of Banu al-Nadir, then ran to Ka‘b ibn Asad, the leader of Banu Qurayzah, whose security pact with the Prophet {{1}} was still in force. Ka‘b, on hearing the news, shut the door of his fortress in Huyayy’s face. Huyayy called, open the door. Ka‘b said, you are an ill-omened man; I have made a pact with Muhammad, I have found nothing from him but honesty and faithfulness, I will not break this pact. Huyayy said, are you keeping the door shut in fear that I will share even a meal of yours? Angered by this, Ka‘b opened the door. Huyayy said, I have brought you the greatest force of the age, an army like a flood; Quraysh has come with its leaders, Ghatafan too with its leaders; they have promised not to return until they wipe out Muhammad and his companions. Ka‘b said, you have brought a cloud of disgrace, thundering within, with no rain; spare me, I have seen nothing from Muhammad but honesty and faithfulness. Huyayy still persisted, kept saying the same thing again and again, in the end Ka‘b agreed on the condition that if Quraysh and Ghatafan returned unable to do anything to Muhammad, Huyayy would take shelter with him in his fortress, whatever came upon him would come upon Huyayy too. In this way Ka‘b broke the pact.{{2}}
blocks.37: When the news reached the Prophet {{1}}, he sent Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) (leader of the Aws), Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) (leader of the Khazraj), ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) and Khawwat ibn Jubayr (RA) to verify. He said, see whether the news is true; if true, tell by hint, do not break people’s morale; if false, say it openly. They went and saw that Banu Qurayzah were saying openly insulting words, denying even the Messenger of Allah {{2}}. Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) cursed them, they came back and told by hint, the news is true. The Prophet {{3}} said, Allahu Akbar, take the good news, O Muslims.{{4}}
blocks.38: The Muslims were caught in a siege from two sides, enemies front and back. The Qur’an describes this moment thus,
blocks.40: Remember when they came upon you from above and from below, and when eyes were bulging and hearts rose to the throats, and you began to think various thoughts about Allah. Then the believers were severely tested and were shaken with a violent shaking.{{1}}
blocks.41: ‘A’ishah (RA) used to say, this verse is about the day of the Trench.{{1}}
blocks.42: Excitement, siege, fear of treachery inside our own home; when fear reaches such a limit, then it is known how deeply someone’s faith is set. ‘Ali (RA) used to say, on the day of the Trench the enemies kept us so busy that we could not pray the middle prayer, ‘Asr, until the sun set. The Prophet {{1}} said, may Allah fill their houses and graves with fire, as they kept us busy from the middle prayer.{{2}}
blocks.43: The Prophet {{1}} made du‘a again and again against the enemies,
blocks.45: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, swift in reckoning, defeat the Confederates. O Allah, defeat them, shake them.{{1}}
blocks.46: One day ‘Umar (RA) came, cursing the disbelievers of Quraysh, and said, O Messenger of Allah, the sun almost set while I was praying ‘Asr. The Prophet {{1}} said, by Allah, I have not prayed it either. Then they went to Buthan, made wudu’, prayed ‘Asr after sunset, then Maghrib.{{2}}
blocks.47: A person who is himself tired, hungry, surrounded by danger, yet is most pained by a prayer slipping away, nothing more is needed to understand where his priority lay.

footnotes.0: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Ghazwat al-Khandaq aw al-Ahzab’ (the instigation of Banu al-Nadir, the formation of the combined army). Sirah-based.
footnotes.1: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Ghazwat al-Khandaq’ (the proposal of Salman al-Farisi (RA)). Sirah-based.
footnotes.2: Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk (through Qudamah ibn ‘Abdillah ibn ‘Amr al-Muzani, the account of the division of forty cubits per ten men). Sirah-based.
footnotes.3: Ma‘arif al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Shafi‘; English edition), vol. 7, introductory part of Surah al-Ahzab, pp. 112–113 (quoted through al-Qurtubi and al-Mazhari).
footnotes.4: Sahih al-Bukhari 4106 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA), through Abu Ishaq); in close wording also in Sahih al-Bukhari 4108–4110.
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari 4099, 4100 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA), through two different chains, close narrations of the same event)
footnotes.10: Imam al-Bayhaqi, Dala’il al-Nubuwwah (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) through Maymun ibn Astadh) ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah. Ibn Kathir himself wrote ‘hadithun gharibun, tafarrada bihi Maymun ibn Astadh’ (this is a gharib hadith narrated through a single chain). There are three more different narrations on the same subject through various chains (al-Nasa’i: Persia-Rome-Abyssinia, through an unknown Companion; al-Tabarani: Persia-Rome-Himyar, through the weak narrator ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An‘um; al-Tabarani-Ibn ‘Abbas: Sham-Persia), each weak or gharib in chain, none sahih. In the detailed lists of cities of conquest there are also discrepancies among the narrations themselves.
footnotes.11: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 2371; Shama’il al-Tirmidhi 134 (from Abu Talhah (RA), through Sayyar ibn Hatim ← Sahl ibn Aslam ← Yazid ibn Abi Mansur ← Anas ibn Malik (RA)). Imam al-Tirmidhi himself called it ‘gharib, I do not know it except through this one chain’; later muhaddithun (the al-Albani/‘Ali Za’i line) called it hasan. The wording of the hadith does not directly contain ‘on the day of the Trench’; the Sirah tradition, according to context, joins it to the account of the hunger of the Trench, and the dars also uses it that way.
footnotes.14: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (the Muslim army three thousand, back toward Mount Sal‘). Sirah-based.
footnotes.15: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh bi-Mujtama‘ al-Asyal Yawm al-Khandaq’ (the full conversation of Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka‘b ibn Asad, Banu Qurayzah’s breach of pact). Sirah-based.
footnotes.16: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Fasl Nuzul Quraysh’ (the delegation of Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh, Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah and Khawwat ibn Jubayr (RA)). Sirah-based.
footnotes.17: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Ahzab 33:10–11, p. 71 (Taqi ‘Uthmani; checked against the rendered PDF).
footnotes.19: Sahih al-Bukhari 4111 (from ‘Ali (RA)); in Sahih al-Bukhari 4112 ‘Umar (RA)’s narration of the same event, with the account of going to Buthan and making up the prayer.
footnotes.21: Sahih al-Bukhari 4112 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA), narrating the event of ‘Umar (RA)).

quiz.q: Who gave the proposal to dig the trench?
How many cubits of trench was each group of ten Companions given to dig?
While carrying earth, in whose rhythm did the Prophet ﷺ recite?
How old was ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA) on the day of Uhud?
Why did the Prophet ﷺ readily accept Salman’s (RA) proposal?
o: He looked at whether the idea was useful

quiz.q: What lesson of leadership comes from the Prophet’s ﷺ digging earth with his own hands?
o: A leader does not work, only gives orders
A leader has to be in front only for show
When a leader is the example, followers are inspired
This was only the need of that era

quiz.q: What was the essence of the Prophet’s ﷺ du‘a on the day of the Trench?
o: The real life is the life of the Hereafter

quiz.q: What did the Companions essentially say in reply to the Prophet’s ﷺ du‘a?
o: That they had pledged allegiance for jihad
That they would pray to Allah for provision
A claim of not being hungry

quiz.q: What was tied to the Prophet’s ﷺ belly when breaking the hard rock?
How many stones did ordinary Companions tie to their bellies to bear hunger?
quiz.e: A Sirah-based comparison, with the Prophet’s ﷺ two.

quiz.q: The Prophet ﷺ had two stones on his belly, the Companions one each; what does this comparison mean?
o: The leader is first in the share of hardship
The lack of food was equal for all
The Prophet ﷺ was only hungrier

quiz.q: What can be learned in today’s life from that moment of du‘a and reply?
o: In hardship one should only complain
One should always make demands of the leader
Giving a promise by mouth is enough
Even in hardship we can give to one another

quiz.q: What was in Jabir’s (RA) home with which the hospitality was made?
o: A sa‘ of barley and a young goat
Some milk and a little honey

quiz.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ essentially tell Jabir’s (RA) wife, through him, to do?
o: Cook even more food and keep it ready
Not take the pot and bread off the stove

quiz.q: What was the state after eating at Jabir’s home?
o: All the food had run out
More food had to be brought

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ call everyone to Jabir’s house, when Jabir had spoken of one or two people?
o: Because he did not even hear Jabir’s request
Because he relied only on blessing
Jabir was too shy to say

quiz.q: From Jabir’s small arrangement, what can be learned about hospitality?
o: One can host even with little, trusting in blessing
Guests should not be invited without a very big arrangement
Hospitality is always the work of the rich
Invitations must be given counting the food

quiz.q: How did Ka‘b ibn Asad, the leader of Banu Qurayzah, first behave with Huyayy?
o: Agreed to the proposal at once

quiz.q: Which prayer was missed on the day of the Trench?
Which verse of Surah al-Ahzab, according to ‘A’ishah (RA), describes the fear of the day of the Trench?
Why did Ka‘b ibn Asad in the end agree to break the pact?
o: Because he had received a large sum of money
The Prophet ﷺ had permitted it
Because of Huyayy’s continuous pressure and instigation
Banu Qurayzah had agreed on this from the start

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell the delegation to report by hint?
o: Because the enemies would have heard
So that morale would not collapse

quiz.q: What can be learned from Ka‘b’s initial firmness?
o: No one should ever be let into one’s house
Firmness breaks down if pressure cannot be handled
One should not talk to a neighbour at all
It is good to decide in a fit of anger
quiz.e: A lesson from Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir.

quiz.q: What can be learned today from the Companions’ pain over the ‘Asr prayer?
o: Even if prayed later slowly, there is no great harm
Even in busyness prayer must be given the most importance
Work is more important than prayer
